clue.text: Gets going, sorting out mostly tricky tasks

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter
sorting out puts things into a fresh order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gets a project moving by dealing with the awkward jobs first.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick-start something is to set it in motion with a sudden push, so kick-starts means gets going.

clue.text: Some like pistols and military caps

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a part of their letters is used

parts.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: A collector fancies both firearms and army headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: A kepi is the flat-topped, peaked cap worn by French soldiers, so the plural fits caps.

clue.text: One seen in vehicle round capital

indicators.note: seen in places one item inside the other

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone is spotted driving about a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo is the capital city of Egypt.

clue.text: Martyr condemned segregation

indicators.note: something condemned is wrecked or broken up, so its letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A martyr spoke out against keeping races apart.
explanation.definitionFit: England's patron saint was, by tradition, a soldier executed for his Christian faith around AD 303.

clue.text: Against carrying on, old sea captain in Twelfth Night

indicators.note: something carrying another holds it within itself

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A list of character notes about a Shakespeare sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying on' looks like a phrase meaning continuing; 'carrying' is the signal and 'on' the contents.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's comedy Twelfth Night, Antonio is the sea captain who rescues and befriends Sebastian.

clue.text: Small child in shade pocketing fancy toy

indicators.note: fancy means elaborately made up, so the letters are arranged afresh
pocketing means putting something away inside

parts.note: a tint is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A little one sits in the shadows, quietly slipping a lovely toy into a pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny tot is an informal phrase for a very young child.

clue.text: Silence leader in Africa, slightly mad

parts.note: to gag someone is to silence them

indicators.note: the leader is whoever goes in front, so only the opening letter is kept

explanation.surface: A call to muzzle an African ruler who seems unhinged.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga is informal for being a little crazy or senile.

clue.text: One's hard to find, and keys a châtelaine lost

indicators.note: lost suggests things gone astray and jumbled up, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: The lady of the house has mislaid her keys, which will be tricky to locate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' looks like a link word, but its three letters belong to the fodder. A châtelaine is the mistress of a large house, who traditionally carried its keys.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names anything practically impossible to locate among a mass of other things.

clue.text: See 7
Is help in it misplaced for one who's lowbrow?

indicators.note: misplaced means put in the wrong position, so the letters move around

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether help is wasted on an uncultured person.
explanation.definitionFit: A philistine is a person hostile or indifferent to culture and the arts.

clue.text: Huge Greek character losing face

indicators.note: the face is the front, so the word drops its first letter

parts.note: the last letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A towering figure from Greece suffers a public humiliation.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is slang for enormous or tremendous.

clue.text: What on-course bookmakers may be doing, talking too loudly

definitions.text: What on-course bookmakers may be doing
definitions.meaning: literal meaning: calling out the betting prices at a racecourse
figurative meaning: speaking boisterously and insistently

explanation.walkthrough: The bookmakers' literal practice has become a British idiom for loud, opinionated talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Trackside bookies once bellowed prices to punters, so the phrase now describes anyone holding forth noisily.

clue.text: I flew free to foreign landmark

indicators.note: foreign means strange or unfamiliar, so the letters are made into something different

explanation.surface: A traveller boasts of a free flight to see a sight overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like the anagram signal, but it belongs to the fodder; 'foreign' does the work, and also hints the landmark is abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The wrought-iron tower in Paris is one of the world's most famous monuments.

clue.text: Overlooks foliage -blossoming

parts.note: flowers that are blossoming are out

explanation.surface: A tree looks over its leaves as they burst into flower.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave out is to omit, which is to overlook or fail to include.

clue.text: Completely secure merchandise, a brand new line about to be introduced

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are formed into another order
to be introduced means further letters are brought into the mix before it is stirred

parts.note: stock is goods held for sale
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A shop locks up its goods while a new product line is about to launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brand new' reads as a single phrase, but 'brand' is fodder and 'new' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names every part of a gun, so it means entirely or in every respect.

clue.text: See 13
Goddess Jeffrey Archer's captured

indicators.note: captured means held inside, so the letters lie within the words

explanation.surface: The novelist Jeffrey Archer has written about a goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Freya is the Norse deity of love and fertility.

clue.text: Cried out for a drink

indicators.note: out suggests being put out of order, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone shouted an order for a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Cider is an alcoholic beverage made from fermented apple juice.

clue.text: Former queen with gift, reportedly, as writer

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a queen

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard by others, so a word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a knack is a gift or talent

explanation.surface: A one-time queen with a talent is said to have become an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Pasternak was the Russian author of Doctor Zhivago.

clue.text: Talk at tedious length about the Spanish clergyman

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: to prate is to chatter on boringly

explanation.surface: A long-winded sermon about the Spanish from a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a high-ranking churchman such as a bishop.

clue.text: Develop image at college

parts.note: a shape is a form or image
a student at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: A student works on their public image while at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To shape up is to progress or turn out, so it means to develop.

clue.text: Expression of views about split in government agency abroad

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: to split is slang for to leave

explanation.surface: A comment about a rift inside a foreign government.
explanation.definitionFit: The State Department is the US government's foreign ministry, hence an agency abroad from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Strange and frightening eastern lake

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
Lake Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A creepy body of water in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie describes something uncanny that inspires unease.

clue.text: Sip drop of sherry in gallery

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, so only a single opening letter is used

explanation.surface: Someone takes a small mouthful of sherry at an art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A taste is a small sample of drink, so a sip.

clue.text: Monster, as a result, returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read from end to start

explanation.surface: A monster came back as a consequence.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore.

clue.text: What may be turned on if one's down in a pumping station?

definitions.text: What may be turned on if one's down
definitions.meaning: informal meaning: tears, which a sad person may start crying
literal meaning: a plant supplying a water system

explanation.walkthrough: 'down' means sad, not lowered; to 'turn on the waterworks' is a British idiom for starting to cry.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a waterworks plant that pumps supplies and, informally, a flood of tears.

clue.text: Garment — king left wearing it

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: wearing means having something on, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A king abandoned a piece of clothing, still putting it on.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilt is the knee-length pleated skirt of Scottish Highland dress.

clue.text: Food store, booming, delivers, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means as it is spoken, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: to deliver someone is to free them

explanation.surface: A grocery with a loud voice makes home deliveries, it is said.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep-freeze is a freezer for storing food at very low temperature.
